newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha lower, ADNOC term talks deadlocked.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha lower, ADNOC term talks deadlocked.

text.p: Near-term naphtha lost ground on Thursday in Tokyo, with prices quoted below $200 per tonne for the first time in nine months, following a sharp loss in crude prices overnight, traders said.
Second-half August open-spec naphtha was offered at $199.50 in afternoon trade against bids at $199.00 after switching hands at $200.00 in early trade.
Open-spec naphtha prices have mostly been in a downward trend since January on the back of weaker global crude oil markets and an influx of arbitrage cargoes from the West.

Naphtha term talks between Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) and its east Asian buyers were said to be deadlocked, with the latest offer price at $21.00 per tonne over the ADNOC formula against bids at $20.00.
"We are unwilling to pay anything more than $20," a trader with one of the potential buyers said.
In low sulphur waxy residue trading for July, sentiment was said to be bullish for sellers as Indonesian allocation is expected to be as small as three million barrels for the month.
On the demand side, however, requirements from Japanese power firms are expected to be sluggish due to high stocks.
